rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes both options for Hafs through Amr al-Sabbah and Hisham through al-Hulwani, relying on the Iraqi routes’ established transmission of short madd.
rows.anchor: عن حفص من طريق عمرو بن الصباح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For al-Asbahani from Warsh he takes both lengths, as for Qalun: both are explicitly transmitted, although short madd is more famous; he does not mix unestablished routes.
rows.anchor: لثبوت الوجهين جميعا عنه نصا كما ذكرنا من الأئمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He uses full, unexaggerated madd in both categories for Hamza, Warsh through al-Azraq, and Ibn Dhakwan through al-Akhfash.
rows.anchor: لحمزة وورش من طريق الأزرق على السواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For readers who lengthen separated madd by an intermediate degree, he also uses an intermediate degree in connected madd for all readers who otherwise shorten it.
rows.anchor: لسائر القراء ممن مد المنفصل بالتوسط في المرتبتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In his graded scheme, short separated madd belongs to Ibn Kathir, Abu Jafar, and disputed readers such as Qalun and Abu Amr; connected madd rises slightly for the short-madd group.
rows.anchor: كابن كثير وأبي جعفر وأصحاب الخلاف كقالون وأبي عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His next degrees rise slightly for al-Kisai, Khalaf, and Ibn Amir, then Asim, then Hamza, Warsh, and al-Akhfash from Ibn Dhakwan’s Iraqi route; only those who pause on madd exceed them.
rows.anchor: ثم فوقها قليلا للكسائي وخلف ولابن عامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He allows graded lengths in both madd categories or only separated madd; under the latter method connected madd stays uniformly full, and he generally chooses the majority position on necessary madd.
rows.anchor: فإن مراتبه عندي في المنفصل كما ذكرت آنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He varied the order while gathering readings with Abu al-Maali ibn al-Labban because that teacher had exceptional recall; this flexible method suits only similarly capable pupils.
rows.anchor: وكنت أنوع بمثل هذه التنويعات حالة الجمع على أبي المعالي بن اللبان لأنه كان أقوى من لقيت استحضارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pupil with weaker recall should follow one fixed sequence, which makes the material easier to retrieve and retain.
rows.anchor: أما من كان ضعيفا في الاستحضار فينبغي أن يسلك به نوعا واحدا من الترتيب لا يزول عنه

rows.speaker: الناس
rows.claim: Many readers start with Qalun because the famous manuals place him first.
rows.anchor: وكثير من الناس يرى تقديم قالون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others begin with Warsh through al-Azraq because his many distinctive modes make it practical to start with long madd, then medium, then short; this is the author’s choice.
rows.anchor: الاختيار. وهذا الذي أختاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When using a fixed sequence, he learned only the order taught by his teachers: after Warsh through al-Azraq come al-Asbahani, Qalun, Abu Jafar, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Yaqub, Ibn Amir, Asim, Hamza, al-Kisai, and Khalaf.
rows.anchor: ثم بأبي عمرو، ثم يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ordered reading, complete each reader before moving on, starting with the narrator listed first for each teacher; experienced teachers stopped premature transitions to prevent omissions.
rows.anchor: ولا ينتقل إلى من بعده حتى يكمل من قبل

rows.speaker: بعض شيوخنا
rows.claim: Some teachers gently tapped the ground to prompt a reader to notice what he had missed, then waited or told him he had not yet reached that point.
rows.anchor: يضرب بيده الأرض خفيفا ليتفطن القارئ ما فاته

rows.speaker: بعض الشيوخ
rows.claim: Other teachers let the pupil finish the faces he thought complete before telling him he had not yet finished.
rows.anchor: حتى يكمل الأوجه في زعمه وينتقل في القراءة إلى ما بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the preceding hamza-substitution case, between-between easing is more common than replacement and is the majority reading.
rows.anchor: بين بين في هذا أكثر وأشهر

rows.speaker: الكسائي والباقون
rows.claim: Al-Kisai deletes the hamza throughout the preceding set, while the other readers retain it.
rows.anchor: الكسائي بحذف الهمزة في ذلك كله

rows.speaker: الأصبهاني عن ورش
rows.claim: Al-Asbahani from Warsh eases the second hamza after an interrogative hamza in the listed Afā forms, and also in أفأنت and أفأنتم.
rows.anchor: واختص الأصبهاني، عن ورش بتسهيل الهمزة الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Asbahani from Warsh also eases the second hamza in لأملأن, which occurs in al-Araf, Hud, al-Sajda, and Sad.
rows.anchor: وكذلك سهل الثانية من (لأملأن)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Asbahani from Warsh eases both hamzas in every form of كأن, including كأن لم تغن and forms with doubled or light nūn.
rows.anchor: وكذلك الهمزتين من " كأن " كيف أتت، مشددة أم مخففة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Asbahani route also eases the hamza in تأذن in al-Araf and in اطمأنوا بها in Yunus and اطمأن به in al-Hajj.
rows.anchor: في يونس و (اطمأن به) في الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Asbahani from Warsh eases the hamza in six رأى occurrences: two in Yusuf, two in al-Naml, one in al-Qasas, and one in al-Munafiqun.
rows.anchor: في ستة مواضع (رأيت أحد عشر كوكبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In تأذن in Ibrahim, al-Mustaneer and al-Tajrid and others report verification; al-Hudhali, al-Hafiz, and Abu al-Ala report easing; Abu al-Izz differs by copy, and Abu Muhammad records both.
rows.anchor: واختلف عنه في (تأذن) في إبراهيم

rows.speaker: النهرواني
rows.claim: Al-Nahrawani uniquely reports verified hamza in اطمأن به in al-Hajj and in three specified رأى forms, through the routes named by Ibn Sawwar and others.
rows.anchor: وانفرد النهرواني فيما حكاه ابن سوار

rows.speaker: السبط
rows.claim: Al-Sibt uniquely records both easing and verification in the three rare رأى forms, and also in two other Yusuf-related cases.
rows.anchor: وانفرد السبط في " المبهج " بالوجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hudhali gives unrestricted easing for راتَه and رآها and similar forms, implying a broader rule; the author rejects this as contrary to the other cited routes.
rows.anchor: ومقتضى ذلك تسهيل (رأيت، ورآه)

rows.speaker: الحافظ أبو عمرو الداني
rows.claim: Al-Dani also gives unrestricted easing in his Jami, but that report comes through Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Farisi, outside the author’s transmission routes.
rows.anchor: نصا الحافظ أبو عمرو الداني في جامعه

rows.speaker: الهذلي عن أبي جعفر
rows.claim: Al-Hudhali alone reports easing تأخر in al-Baqara and al-Fath, and أو يتأخر in al-Muddaththir, contrary to the other transmitters.
rows.anchor: وانفرد الهذلي عن أبي جعفر من روايتيه

rows.speaker: الحنبلي عن هبة الله في رواية ابن وردان
rows.claim: Al-Hanbali, through Hibat Allah in Ibn Wardans narration, uniquely reports easing تأذن in both occurrences.
rows.anchor: وانفرد الحنبلي، عن هبة الله في رواية ابن وردان

rows.speaker: البزي
rows.claim: For لعانتم in al-Baqara, most transmitters from Abu Rabia report easing, while al-Tajrid reports verification; both faces are sound from al-Bazzi.
rows.anchor: واختلف عن البزي في تسهيل الهمزة من (لاعنتكم)

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jafar alone deletes the hamza in متكأ in Yusuf, making it read like متقى.
rows.anchor: واختص أبو جعفر بحذف الهمزة في (متكأ)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the discussed lām assimilation, a preceding consonant permits assimilation; with a preceding sukūn and open following vowel it is normally clear, except the frequent lām of قال, which assimilates.
rows.anchor: فإن سكن ما قبلها أدغمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the letter before mīm has a vowel, mīm before bā is made quiescent and concealed with nasalization to avoid successive vowels; when the preceding letter is quiescent, the general rule is to leave it clear.
rows.anchor: تسكن عند الباء إذا تحرك ما قبلها

rows.speaker: القصباني عن شجاع عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: Al-Qasbani from Shuja from Abu Amr reports concealment after a madd or lin letter, but this route is outside the book’s transmissions.
rows.anchor: إلا ما رواه القصباني، عن شجاع، عن أبي عمرو من الإخفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some earlier scholars called this concealment idgham; the author says ikhfa is the correct term and defers fuller discussion.
rows.anchor: وقد عبر بعض المتقدمين عن هذا الإخفاء بالإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nūn assimilates into rāʾ or lām when the preceding letter is vowelled, but remains clear when the preceding letter is quiescent.
rows.anchor: تدغم إذا تحرك ما قبلها في الراء واللام

rows.speaker: أصحاب اليزيدي عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: They assimilate the final nūn of نحن into lām only in ten occurrences; other than this word, a quiescent preceding letter prevents assimilation.
rows.anchor: إلا في كلمة نحن حيث وقعت وجملته عشرة مواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed cause is the heaviness of the ḍamma, but the author counters it with أنى يكون له ولد, where the relevant sound remains clear.
rows.anchor: فقيل لثقل الضمة، ويرد على ذلك

rows.speaker: الداني
rows.claim: Al-Dani explains the exception by the vowel’s permanence and inability to shift away from ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقال الداني: للزوم حركتها

rows.speaker: المدنيان وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: The Medinan readers, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr open the additive yāʾ in six contexts: three إني أخاف occurrences, إني أعظك, إني أعوذ بك, and شقاقي أن.
rows.anchor: فتح الستة المدنيان، وابن كثير وأبو عمرو

rows.speaker: المدنيان وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: The Medinans and Abu Amr open the yāʾ in عني إنه, إني إذا, نصحي إن, and ضيفي أليس.
rows.anchor: فتح الأربعة المدنيان، وأبو عمرو

rows.speaker: المدنيان وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحفص
rows.claim: They open the additive yāʾ in أجري إلا in both places in Hud.
rows.anchor: وأجري إلا في الموضعين فتحهما المدنيان، وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحفص

rows.speaker: المدنيان وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن ذكوان
rows.claim: These readers open the yāʾ in أرهطي أعز.
rows.anchor: أرهطي أعز فتحها المدنيان، وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن ذكوان

rows.speaker: المدنيان والبزي؛ أبو تغلب عن قنبل
rows.claim: The Medinans and al-Bazzi open the yāʾ in فطرني أفلا; Abu Taghlib uniquely reports this from Qunbul through Ibn Shanabudh.
rows.anchor: فطرني أفلا فتحها المدنيان، والبزي، وانفرد أبو تغلب بذلك عن قنبل

rows.speaker: المدنيان والبزي
rows.claim: The Medinans and al-Bazzi open the yāʾ in ولكني أراكم and وإني أراكم.
rows.anchor: ولكني أراكم وإني أراكم فتحهما المدنيان والبزي

rows.speaker: المدنيان
rows.claim: The Medinan readers open the additive yāʾ in إني أشهد الله.
rows.anchor: إني أشهد الله فتحهما المدنيان

rows.speaker: المدنيان وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
rows.claim: The Medinans, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir open the yāʾ in وما توفيقي إلا بالله.
rows.anchor: وما توفيقي إلا بالله فتحها المدنيان، وأبو عمرو وابن عامر

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو وورش ويعقوب
rows.claim: For فلا تسألن, Abu Jafar, Abu Amr, and Warsh retain the extra yāʾ in connected recitation, while Yaqub retains it in both connection and pause; al-Mubhij alone reports it from Qalun through Abu Nashit.
rows.anchor: أثبتها في الوصل أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو وورش، وأثبتها في الحالين يعقوب

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaqub retains the extra yāʾ in ثم لا تنظروني both in connection and at pause.
rows.anchor: ثم لا تنظروني أثبتها في الحالين يعقوب

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وقنبل
rows.claim: Abu Jafar and Abu Amr retain the extra yāʾ in connection in ولا تخزون; Yaqub retains it in both states, and it is also reported for Qunbul through Ibn Shanabudh.
rows.anchor: ولا تخزون أثبتها في الوصل أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو وأثبتها في الحالين يعقوب

rows.speaker: المدنيان وأبو عمرو والكسائي وابن كثير ويعقوب
rows.claim: The Medinans, Abu Amr, and al-Kisai retain the yāʾ in connection at يوم يأت; Ibn Kathir and Yaqub retain it in both states, while the others delete it for ease.
rows.anchor: يوم يأت أثبتها وصلا المدنيان، وأبو عمرو والكسائي، وأثبتها ابن كثير

rows.speaker: الكسائي والباقون
rows.claim: Al-Kisai reads the dāl in بعدا with kasra and tanwin; the other readers use fatḥa without tanwin.
rows.anchor: فقرأ الكسائي بكسر الدال مع التنوين

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي والباقون
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read سلم with kasra and a quiescent lām, without alif, in both passages; the others read سلام with fatḥa and alif.
rows.anchor: حمزة والكسائي، (سلم) بكسر السين

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة وحفص والباقون
rows.claim: Ibn Amir, Hamza, and Hafs read يعقوب in the accusative, while the other readers read it in the nominative.
rows.anchor: ابن عامر وحمزة وحفص بنصب الباء

rows.speaker: المدنيان وابن كثير والباقون
rows.claim: For أسر with the preposition, the Medinans and Ibn Kathir use hamzat al-waṣl at all five locations, joining it after أن and beginning with kasra; the rest use hamzat al-qaṭʿ with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: فقرأ المدنيان، وابن كثير بوصل الألف في الخمسة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والباقون
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr raise the tāʾ in امرأتك; the other readers use the accusative.
rows.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو برفع التاء

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص والباقون
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, Khalaf, and Hafs read أصلاتك as a singular without wāw; the others retain wāw for the plural.
rows.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص بحذف الواو

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص والباقون
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, Khalaf, and Hafs read the sīn in سعدوا with ḍamma; the others use fatḥa.
rows.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص بضم السين

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو بكر والباقون
rows.claim: Nafi, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Bakr read the nūn in وإن كلا as quiescent and light; the remaining readers geminate it.
rows.anchor: فقرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو بكر بإسكان النون مخففة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: Abu Jafar, Ibn Amir, Asim, and Hamza geminate the mīm in لمّا in Hud and al-Tariq; distinct reader groups geminate it in Ya-Sin and al-Zukhruf.
rows.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة بتشديد الميم هنا والطارق

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة وابن جماز؛ عاصم وحمزة وابن جماز
rows.claim: In Ya-Sin, Ibn Amir, Asim, Hamza, and Ibn Jammaz geminate لما; in al-Zukhruf, Asim, Hamza, and Ibn Jammaz do so.
rows.anchor: وشددها في يس لما جميع ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة وابن جماز

rows.speaker: هشام؛ المشارقة وأكثر المغاربة؛ الحافظ أبو عمرو الداني
rows.claim: The eastern transmitters and most westerners report gemination from Hisham by all routes; al-Dani records both light and geminated forms, read the light form through al-Hulwani and Ibn Abbad, and says gemination was Hisham’s choice.
rows.anchor: فروى عنه المشارقة قاطبة، وأكثر المغاربة تشديدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For a final hamza with kasra after kasra, as in من شاطئ and لكل امرئ, he gives three pause forms: substitute a quiet yāʾ by analogy, use a kasra yāʾ per Tamim, or ease between hamza and yāʾ with rawm or follow the written form.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك: (من شاطئ، ولكل امرئ)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a kasra hamza follows fatḥa in a word written with yāʾ, the three forms above plus the analogical alif substitution yield four options.
rows.anchor: وتجئ هذه الأوجه الثلاثة فيما رسم بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For a word written without yāʾ, only alif substitution or eased pronunciation with rawm is allowed; al-Hudhali permits yāʾ in من ملجأ, but the author rejects that as unsound.
rows.anchor: فليس فيه سوى وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For a kasra hamza after ḍamma, as in كأمثال اللؤلؤ, he lists four faces: quiet wāw by analogy, kasra wāw attributed to al-Akhfash, ease between hamza and yāʾ, or the difficult hamza-wāw intermediate on rawm.
rows.anchor: مما وقعت الهمزة فيه مكسورة بعد ضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final ḍamma hamza in يخرج منهما اللؤلؤ has two faces, wāw substitution or easing the final hamza on rawm; with final fatḥa in حسبتهم لؤلؤا, both hamzas become wāw, the first quiet.
rows.anchor: الهمزة الأخيرة فيه مضمومة نحو (يخرج منهما اللؤلؤ)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For an open hamza after fatḥa, as in بدأ and امرأ, he accepts alif substitution; a reported between-between form using rawm is anomalous and not sound.
rows.anchor: مما وقعت الهمزة فيه مفتوحة بعد فتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At pause, treating the accusative like nominative and genitive is a known Arabic usage: replace the hamza with alif and delete it before a following sukūn. Madd, medium length, and qasr follow from possible interpretations of the written alif, though qasr has no clear basis.
rows.anchor: وهو إجراء المنصوب مجرى المرفوع والمجرور، وهو لغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For وأحباوه, the first hamza may be verified or eased and the second eased with madd or qasr; the resulting four or twelve combinations are valid, but extra rasm-based substitutions that would make twenty-four are not sound or permissible.
rows.anchor: ففي همزته الأولى التحقيق والتسهيل؛ لكونها متوسطة بزائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In تراء, the post-hamza alif is deleted in connection and retained at pause; Hamza and Khalaf incline the rāʾ in connection, and Hamza at pause eases and inclines the hamza, with madd or qasr allowed. The author calls this the only valid face.
rows.anchor: وأما تراء من (التقى الجمعان) في سورة الشعراء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A further proposal deletes the alif after the hamza by following the rasm, making the hamza final; this is one of the other faces the author says must not be followed.
rows.anchor: وذكر فيها وجهان آخران، أحدهما: حذف الألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On his first Egyptian journey, he completed a gathered reading with Ibn al-Saigh, starting at al-Hijr on Saturday and finishing the following Thursday night, with the remaining opening of al-Waqia read in one sitting.
rows.anchor: وأدركني السفر كنت قد وصلت في ختمة بالجمع

rows.speaker: أبو بكر محمد بن أحمد بن أبي بكر بن عرام الإسكندري
rows.claim: Ibn Arram, described as a reliable hadith scholar, relayed that Ibn Wathiq came from the Maghrib to teach Makin al-Din al-Asmar the readings; after starting a seven-reading khatma that night, al-Asmar completed it by dawn.
rows.anchor: الشيخ الإمام المحدث الثقة أبو بكر محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A student mastering readings should memorize a complete manual, learn its terminology and routes, recite each reading separately first, then train to gather them after fluency develops.
rows.anchor: من يريد تحقيق علم القراءات وإحكام تلاوة الحروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When gathering, identify differences in principles and individual loci; use one face where readings overlap, connect adjacent variants when possible without strain or improper combination, and otherwise restart so no face is omitted or repeated.
rows.anchor: فما أمكن فيه التداخل اكتفى منه بوجه وما لم يمكن فيه نظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omission is forbidden, improper composition is disliked, and repetition is defective; readers must distinguish permissible variant options from route and narration differences to avoid mixed transmissions.
rows.anchor: فإن الأول ممنوع والثاني مكروه والثالث معيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven inter-sura takbir forms are optional choices, not all compulsory between every pair; when gathering particular transmission routes, however, one must include a form tied to the end, tied to the beginning, or compatible with both.
rows.anchor: ليس الاختلاف في هذه الأوجه السبعة اختلاف رواية يلزم الإتيان بها كلها بين كل سورتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teachers recommended using one of the five forms between each pair to practise them all, but this is not obligatory once the student has learned one from the teacher.
rows.anchor: يأمروننا بأن نأتي بين كل سورتين بوجه من الخمسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When transmitted, tahlil, takbir, and hamdala are joined as one unit without separating their parts; their combinations with the preceding sura, basmala, and following sura follow the takbir’s seven forms.
rows.anchor: التهليل مع التكبير مع الحمدلة عند من رواه، حكمه حكم التكبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He does not recall reciting hamdala after al-Nas; accordingly, with hamdala only the five forms that treat takbir as belonging to the beginning of the next sura are available, though al-Hudhali’s wording does not exclude the other assignment.
rows.anchor: إلا أني لا أعلمني قرأت بالحمدلة بعد سورة الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamdala cannot be used at the beginning of al-Duha because its transmitter does not mention it there.
rows.anchor: نعم يمتنع وجه الحمدلة من أول الضحى لأن صاحبه لم يذكره فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transmitted order of tahlil, takbir, and basmala is mandatory; al-Hudhali’s report from Qunbul through the Nazif route placing basmala before takbir is unknown and unauthenticated because Ibn Ghalbun and the other transmitters do not report it.
rows.anchor: ترتيب التهليل مع التكبير والبسملة على ما ذكرنا لازم لا يجوز مخالفته
